name: C#
summary: Use the C# type system, nullable values, dictionaries, records, and LINQ to build small .NET console programs.

prerequisites: Know how to save a plain text file.
Use a .NET 8 or newer SDK and place each example in Program.cs of a console project. Run it with dotnet run from a terminal. The examples use the standard library.
metadata.miniProject: Build a reading-list report. Parse page counts, store books as records, group by status, and use LINQ to print a sorted list of unfinished books. Handle empty input and malformed counts.

references.title: Microsoft Learn: Inside a C# program

lessons.title: Types, local variables, and interpolation
lessons.explanation: A console app can use top-level statements. C# checks expression types at compile time. A local declared with var gets a type from its initializer. String interpolation places values inside a string.

api.name: var
api.description: Infer a local variable type from its initializer.

lessons.practice: Print the total cost of three tickets at 350 cents each, then change the quantity to five.
lessons.pitfall: A var local still has a specific compile-time type. A value of an incompatible type cannot be assigned later.

references.title: Microsoft Learn: Inside a C# program

exercise.expected: Report a count and a total in integer cents.
exercise.completion: The outputs contain totals of 1050 and 1750 cents for the two counts.

lessons.title: Missing strings and TryParse
lessons.explanation: In a nullable-aware file, string? tells the compiler a reference may be null. Int32.TryParse reports whether conversion succeeded and supplies an integer through an out parameter. Short-circuiting with && keeps the range check on the success path.

api.name: #nullable enable
api.description: Enable nullable reference annotations and analysis in this file.

api.name: string?
api.description: Annotate a string reference that may be null.

api.name: int.TryParse()
api.description: Return a success flag and an integer via an out parameter.

lessons.practice: Accept quantities from 1 through 20. Return a fallback of 2 when the text is missing, malformed, or outside the range.
lessons.pitfall: Nullable reference annotations guide compiler warnings. They do not add a runtime check before you use a reference.

exercise.expected: Safely return a positive quantity or a fallback.

lessons.title: Count values with a dictionary
lessons.explanation: Dictionary<TKey, TValue> maps keys to values. TryGetValue tells you whether a key already exists. For an integer value, the out result defaults to zero when the key is absent. Choose a string comparer to make key equality explicit.

api.name: TryGetValue()
api.description: Read a value and tell whether the key existed.

lessons.practice: Count the words in a small array with a case-insensitive dictionary. Print distinct counts.
lessons.pitfall: Reading a missing key with the indexer throws KeyNotFoundException. TryGetValue handles that case explicitly.

exercise.expected: Treat uppercase and lowercase spellings as the same key for this report.
exercise.completion: The words "tea", "Tea", and "coffee" produce two keys with counts 2 and 1.

lessons.title: Records and non-destructive updates
lessons.explanation: A positional record class generates properties and value equality for its declared data. A with expression makes a shallow copy and sets the properties you name. That helps keep an earlier snapshot available.

api.name: record
api.description: Declare a type that generates value-based equality.

api.name: with
api.description: Copy a record and initialize selected properties.

lessons.practice: Model a Book with a title and page count. Correct one count with with and compare two independent Book values.
lessons.pitfall: A with expression copies references in properties. Both records can still share a mutable collection stored inside them.

exercise.expected: Keep the original record available while creating an updated value.
exercise.completion: The original remains at 120 pages. The updated copy has 128 pages and compares unequal to it.

lessons.title: Filter, sort, and materialize LINQ results
lessons.explanation: Where selects values that satisfy a predicate. OrderBy sorts by a key. These LINQ operations are typically evaluated as you enumerate them. ToArray materializes the values at that point in time.

api.name: Where()
api.description: Filter a sequence with a predicate.

api.name: OrderBy()
api.description: Order elements by a selected key.

api.name: ToArray()
api.description: Evaluate the sequence and return an array.

lessons.practice: Filter the values 11, 2, 8, and 4 to the even values. Sort them descending and print their total.
lessons.pitfall: Holding the query alone does not take a snapshot of mutable source data. Materialize it when you need stable results.

exercise.expected: Print the sorted sequence of selected values and its sum.
exercise.completion: The output sequence is 8, 4, 2 and the total is 14.
